self_corrections.reason: IMPOSSIBLE_TYPING_SPEED metric compares inter-visit intervals against human keyboard input speed. Browser page-load events are not typing events. A human clicking a search result link produces sub-second page loads without automation.

infer_intent is designed for conversational manipulation patterns (jailbreaks, gradual escalation). Browser history is not a conversation. GRADUAL_ESCALATION from URL length growth is a structural artifact, not manipulation.

macOS SQLite and bplist files are binary by design. Purgatory correctly seals them. This is NOT tampering or malformation. The forensic_alert text is a template applied to all binary files and should not be treated as an anomaly signal for standard macOS artifacts.

findings.title: Counter-forensics reconnaissance — Autopsy DFIR platform
findings.firstness: 9 Safari visits to 'autopsey'/'autopsy' queries in a 14-second window on 2019-10-16 17:45 UTC. Typo-correction sequence (3x autopsey → 6x autopsy). WAL file confirms URLs present in active journal.
findings.secondness: Normal employees do not research open-source DFIR platforms (Autopsy, by Brian Carrier — used by law enforcement). Typo-correction sequence is a behavioral signature of active, intentional research rather than incidental navigation. Sub-second repeated hits are browser history deduplication artifacts, not automation.
findings.thirdness: Subject is assessing what digital forensic investigators can extract from macOS evidence. This is reconnaissance against the forensic toolchain — understanding the adversary's detection capability before taking operational action. Carnegie: authority-transfer countermeasure (disarm the analyst's tools).
findings.devil_advocate: Tuck Gorge is an IT professional evaluating Autopsy for legitimate incident response use at M57.Biz. Autopsy is freely available and commonly assessed by sysadmins. Typo-correction is normal human behavior. STRENGTH: MEDIUM. REBUTTAL: Legitimate IT autopsy evaluation would involve visiting autopsy's project page, documentation, and release notes — not rapid repeated Google search hits in a 14-second burst. The visit pattern is consistent with someone who just heard the name and needs to verify it, not an IT professional doing procurement evaluation.
findings.corroboration: F-002 — VPN research 31.3h later establishes temporal OPSEC sequence coherence
findings.daubert_gate: Two independent sources (Safari History + WAL confirmation). INTENT threshold met.

findings.title: VPN-over-HTTP research chain → SoftEther NAT traversal deployment planning
findings.firstness: 9.4-minute session 2019-10-18 00:53–01:03 UTC. Google search 'vpn software that runs over http' → softether.org → serverfault/askubuntu VPN-over-HTTP threads → Wikipedia SoftEther article → openvpn.net and radmin-vpn (comparison) → howstuffworks VPN article → SoftEther mobile docs (Windows/Mac laptops) → softether-download.com (4 visits, 26 seconds) → L2TP/IPsec setup guide → NAT traversal + Dynamic DNS configuration (final destination). Shannon entropy of URL corpus: 4.97 bits/byte (NOISE — legitimate domains, no C2 obfuscation).
findings.secondness: Search term 'vpn software that runs over http' is operationally specific — targets HTTP tunneling capability, not general remote access. Navigation terminates at NAT traversal documentation (server-side configuration), not client setup guides. Normal employee VPN use terminates at client configuration. Server-side deployment planning is anomalous for a regular M57.Biz employee.
findings.thirdness: Subject is planning deployment of a covert communications channel: SoftEther VPN operating over HTTPS/SSTP, designed to be indistinguishable from normal web traffic by network monitors and DPI systems. Combined with F-001 (31.3h prior), this is Phase 2 of a two-stage OPSEC sequence: (1) assess what forensics detects, (2) deploy a channel forensics cannot easily trace. Carnegie: institutional trust exploitation — HTTPS VPN traffic is indistinguishable from web browsing to network monitors, bypassing corporate DLP and firewall logging.
findings.carnegie: Institutional trust exploitation — HTTP/HTTPS VPN bypasses network monitoring by mimicking legitimate traffic
findings.devil_advocate: Tuck Gorge is an IT professional setting up a home VPN for remote access to M57.Biz resources, or for personal privacy while traveling. SoftEther is a legitimate product used by thousands of IT professionals. NAT traversal docs are relevant to anyone deploying a home server. STRENGTH: MEDIUM. REBUTTAL: (a) Legitimate remote access VPN at M57.Biz would be configured by IT, not by an employee researching it on their personal Mac. (b) The search term 'vpn software that runs over http' specifically targets firewall evasion — a legitimate VPN user searches for 'best vpn for remote work'. (c) Reading NAT traversal server docs (not client docs) indicates server deployment, not client usage.
findings.corroboration: F-001 (Autopsy research 31.3h prior). MACOS_FORENSICS pipeline z=1.600, exit_code=3. reason_with_llm verdict=INTENT (70%).
findings.daubert_gate: Two independent sources + reason_with_llm corroboration. INTENT threshold met.

findings.title: Browser diversification — Chrome x2 + Firefox within 21 days
findings.firstness: 4 quarantine events: NYT image (2019-07-12, Chrome), Firefox 68.0.2 (2019-08-17, Chrome), Chrome stable (2019-08-19, Chrome), Chrome stable re-download (2019-09-08, Chrome). Two Chrome downloads within 21 days. Firefox downloaded day after first Chrome install.
findings.secondness: Browser cycling within 21 days is anomalous for regular users. Firefox installed day after Chrome download suggests browser compartmentalization testing.
findings.thirdness: Browser cycling is an OPSEC technique: using different browsers for different activity categories to compartmentalize browsing history, cookies, and fingerprints. Insufficient to confirm without per-browser session attribution.
findings.devil_advocate: Chrome auto-update failure requiring manual re-download. Firefox for a specific site. Standard user behavior. STRENGTH: HIGH.
findings.corroboration: F-001 and F-002 are thematically coherent with browser compartmentalization as an OPSEC technique. Insufficient independent confirmation for INTENT.
findings.daubert_gate: Single artifact class. Capped at SUSPICION.
